#### Read in the data
```{r reading the data}

# Load the mRNA count matrices
mg1.umi <- Read10X("/links/groups/treutlein/DATA/sequencing/20220825_P2092_MARINA_Mg_opt_and_BVO_HTO_repeat/processed/MG_opt_1/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/")
mg2.umi <- Read10X("/links/groups/treutlein/DATA/sequencing/20220825_P2092_MARINA_Mg_opt_and_BVO_HTO_repeat/processed/MG_opt_2/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/")

# Save the mRNA count natrices as rds files
saveRDS(mg1.umi, "Objects/Protocol_optimization/mg1_umi_mtx.rds")
saveRDS(mg1.umi, "Objects/Protocol_optimization/mg2_umi_mtx.rds")

# Load the HTO count matrices
hto1 <- readRDS("Objects/Protocol_optimization/hto1_mtx.rds")
hto2 <- readRDS("Objects/Protocol_optimization/hto2_mtx.rds")

# Check the number of cells
ncol(mg1.umi) # 10651
ncol(mg2.umi) # 10903

```

```{r prepare mRNA matrices}

# The column names (cells) have an additional "-1" which is not present in the HTO counts
# To allow for joining of the common barcodes in both matrices, we rename the barcodes by removing the additional "-1" pattern
colnames_mg1 <- colnames(mg1.umi)
colnames_mg1 <- gsub("-1", "", colnames_mg1)
colnames(mg1.umi) <- colnames_mg1

colnames_mg2 <- colnames(mg2.umi)
colnames_mg2 <- gsub("-1", "", colnames_mg2)
colnames(mg2.umi) <- colnames_mg2

```


#### Generate joint barcode matrices
```{r joint matrices}

# Select cell barcodes detected by both RNA and HTO 
mg1.joint.bcs <- intersect(colnames(mg1.umi), colnames(hto1))
mg2.joint.bcs <- intersect(colnames(mg2.umi), colnames(hto2))

# Check how many cells have an assigned barcode
table(colnames(mg1.umi) %in% colnames(hto1))
#FALSE  TRUE 
#  816  9835 
  
table(colnames(mg2.umi) %in% colnames(hto2))
#FALSE  TRUE 
#  987  9916 
  
# Subset RNA and HTO counts by joint cell barcodes
mg1.umi <- mg1.umi[, mg1.joint.bcs]
mg2.umi <- mg2.umi[, mg2.joint.bcs]

hto1 <- as.matrix(hto1[, mg1.joint.bcs])
hto2 <- as.matrix(hto2[, mg2.joint.bcs])

# Confirm that the HTO have the correct names
rownames(hto1)
rownames(hto2)

```

#### Setup Seurat object and add in the HTO data
```{r setup seurat with HTO}

# Setup Seurat object
mg1.hashtag <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = mg1.umi, project = "Replicate1")
mg2.hashtag <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = mg2.umi, project = "Replicate2")

# Normalize, find variable features, scale the data and run PCA on the RNA data with log normalization
mg1.hashtag <- NormalizeData(mg1.hashtag) 
mg2.hashtag <- NormalizeData(mg2.hashtag) 

```

# Demultiplex cells based on HTO enrichment
#### Add HTO as an indepent assay to the Seurat object
```{r add HTO data}

# Add HTO data as a new assay independent from RNA
mg1.hashtag[["HTO"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = hto1)
mg2.hashtag[["HTO"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = hto2)

# Normalize HTO data, here we use centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation
mg1.hashtag <- NormalizeData(mg1.hashtag, assay = "HTO", normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2)
mg2.hashtag <- NormalizeData(mg2.hashtag, assay = "HTO", normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2)


# Important about normalization
# Normalization of the data leads to vastly different results, I tested this.
# For CLR (centered log ratio), one can choose margin = 1 (normalize across features) or margin = 2 (normalize across cells). 
# According to people from Satija lab, in some cases, cell-based normalization fails. 
# This is because cell-normalization makes an assumption that the total ADT/HTO counts should be constant across cells. 
# That can become a significant issue if you have cell populations in your data, but did not add protein markers for them (this is also an issue for scRNA-seq, but is significantly mitigated because at least you measure many genes).
# However, gene-based normalization can fail when there is significant heterogeneity in sequencing depth, or cell size. The optimal strategy depends on the AB panel, and heterogeneity of the sample.
# It is wise to try both across features and across genes, as I did here. Unfortunately, there is no one clear and correct answer...

```

#### Demultiplex using the Seurat function HTODemux() to assign single cells back to their sample origins
```{r demultiplex}

# If one has a very large dataset Seurat suggests using k_function = 'clara'. 
# This is a k-medoid clustering function for large applications 
# One can also play with additional parameters (see documentation for HTODemux()) to adjust the threshold for classification 
# Here I am using the default settings
mg1.hashtag <- HTODemux(mg1.hashtag, assay = "HTO", positive.quantile = 0.99)
mg2.hashtag <- HTODemux(mg2.hashtag, assay = "HTO", positive.quantile = 0.99)

```

# Visualization
#### Output from running HTODemux() is saved in the object metadata
#### We can visualize how many cells are classified as singlets, doublets and negative/ambiguous cells
```{r visualize HTO classification}

# Global classification results
table(mg1.hashtag$HTO_classification.global)
# Doublet Singlet 
#    1556    8279 
table(mg2.hashtag$HTO_classification.global) 
# Doublet Negative  Singlet 
#    1795      137     7984 

# Change the order to display the hashtags 
hto_order <- c("Doublet", "HTO1", "HTO2", "HTO3", "HTO4", "HTO5", "HTO6", "HTO7", "HTO8", "HTO9", "HTO10", "HTO13", "Negative")
mg1.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID <- factor(mg1.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID, levels = hto_order)
mg2.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID <- factor(mg2.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID, levels = hto_order)

# Group cells based on the max HTO signal
mg1.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID <- factor(mg1.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID, levels = hto_order)
Idents(mg1.hashtag) <- "HTO_maxID"
RidgePlot(mg1.hashtag, assay = "HTO", features = rownames(mg1.hashtag[["HTO"]])[1:12], ncol = 4)

mg2.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID <- factor(mg2.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID, levels = hto_order)
Idents(mg2.hashtag) <- "HTO_maxID"
RidgePlot(mg2.hashtag, assay = "HTO", features = rownames(mg2.hashtag[["HTO"]])[1:12], ncol = 4)
   
```

#### Compare number of UMIs for singlets, doublets and negative cells
```{r QC of HTOs}

global.order <- c("Singlet", "Doublet", "Negative")
mg1.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_classification.global <- factor(mg1.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_classification.global, levels = global.order)
mg2.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_classification.global <- factor(mg2.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_classification.global, levels = global.order)

# Assign the droplets singlets, doublets or negative identities
Idents(mg1.hashtag) <- "HTO_classification.global"
Idents(mg2.hashtag) <- "HTO_classification.global"

# Plot UMI counts 
VlnPlot(mg1.hashtag, features = "nCount_RNA", pt.size = 0.1, log = TRUE)
VlnPlot(mg2.hashtag, features = "nCount_RNA", pt.size = 0.1, log = TRUE)
```

#### Exclude HTO2 (the alternative to FBS as this condition does not fit into the experimental setup and idea and we are not interested in analysing it further for the moment)
```{r exclude HTO2}

# Remove HTO2 
mg1.hashtag <- subset(mg1.hashtag, subset = HTO_maxID == "HTO2", invert = T)
mg2.hashtag <- subset(mg2.hashtag, subset = HTO_maxID == "HTO2", invert = T)

# Change the order to display the hashtags 
hto_order <- c("Doublet", "HTO1", "HTO3", "HTO4", "HTO5", "HTO6", "HTO7", "HTO8", "HTO9", "HTO10", "HTO13", "Negative")
mg1.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID <- factor(mg1.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID, levels = hto_order)
mg2.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID <- factor(mg2.hashtag@meta.data$hash.ID, levels = hto_order)

# Group cells based on the max HTO signal
mg1.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID <- factor(mg1.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID, levels = hto_order)
Idents(mg1.hashtag) <- "HTO_maxID"
rep1 <- RidgePlot(mg1.hashtag, assay = "HTO", features = rownames(mg1.hashtag[["HTO"]])[c(2:11)], ncol = 4, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10))

mg2.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID <- factor(mg2.hashtag@meta.data$HTO_maxID, levels = hto_order)
Idents(mg2.hashtag) <- "HTO_maxID"
rep2 <- RidgePlot(mg2.hashtag, assay = "HTO", features = rownames(mg2.hashtag[["HTO"]])[c(2:11)], ncol = 4, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10))
  
pdf("Plots/Protocol_optimization/HTOs_expression_per_replicate.pdf", height = 16, width = 15)
rep1 / rep2
dev.off()

```

#### Generate a two dimensional tSNE embedding for HTOs.Here we are grouping cells by singlets and doublets for simplicity
```{r 2D embedding of HTOs}

# First, we will remove negative cells and doubletsfrom the object
mg1.hashtag.subset <- mg1.hashtag
mg2.hashtag.subset <- subset(mg2.hashtag, idents = "Negative", invert = TRUE)

# Calculate a tSNE embedding of the HTO data
# For each replicate separately
DefaultAssay(mg1.hashtag.subset) <- "HTO"
DefaultAssay(mg2.hashtag.subset) <- "HTO"

mg1.hashtag.subset <- ScaleData(mg1.hashtag.subset, features = rownames(mg1.hashtag.subset), verbose = FALSE) %>% 
                      RunPCA(features = rownames(mg1.hashtag.subset), approx = FALSE) %>%
                      RunTSNE(dims = 1:8, perplexity = 100, check_duplicates = FALSE)
mg2.hashtag.subset <- ScaleData(mg2.hashtag.subset, features = rownames(mg2.hashtag.subset), verbose = FALSE) %>% 
                      RunPCA(features = rownames(mg2.hashtag.subset), approx = FALSE) %>%
                      RunTSNE(dims = 1:8, perplexity = 100, check_duplicates = FALSE)

Idents(mg1.hashtag.subset) <- "HTO_classification.global"
Idents(mg2.hashtag.subset) <- "HTO_classification.global"
DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset) 

# One can also visualize the more detailed classification result by running Idents(object) <- 'HTO_classification' before plotting. 
# Here, one can see that each of the small clouds on the tSNE plot corresponds to one of the 28 possible doublet combinations.
Idents(mg1.hashtag.subset) <- 'hash.ID' 
Idents(mg2.hashtag.subset) <- 'hash.ID' 
( DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset, cols = c("gray",vintage_rich_cols(10))) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset, cols = c("gray",vintage_rich_cols(10))) )

pdf("Plots/Protocol_optimization/umap_HTOs.pdf", width = 9, height = 5)
( DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset, cols = c("gray",vintage_rich_cols(10)), pt.size = 0.4) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset, cols = c("gray",vintage_rich_cols(10)), pt.size = 0.4) )
dev.off()

png("Plots/Protocol_optimization/umap_HTOs.png", width = 4200, height = 2200, res = 480)
( DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset, cols = c("gray",vintage_rich_cols(10)), pt.size = 0.4) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset, cols = c("gray",vintage_rich_cols(10)), pt.size = 0.4) )
dev.off()

```


#### Generate a two dimensional tSNE embedding for HTOs without doublets
```{r 2D embedding of HTOs without doublets}

# First, we will remove negative cells and doublets from the object
Idents(mg1.hashtag) <- "HTO_classification.global"
mg1.hashtag.subset <- mg1.hashtag
mg1.hashtag.subset <- subset(mg1.hashtag.subset, idents = "Singlet")
Idents(mg2.hashtag) <- "HTO_classification.global"
mg2.hashtag.subset <- subset(mg2.hashtag, idents = "Negative", invert = TRUE)
mg2.hashtag.subset <- subset(mg2.hashtag.subset, idents = "Singlet")

# Calculate a tSNE embedding of the HTO data
# For each replicate separately
DefaultAssay(mg1.hashtag.subset) <- "HTO"
DefaultAssay(mg2.hashtag.subset) <- "HTO"

mg1.hashtag.subset <- ScaleData(mg1.hashtag.subset, features = rownames(mg1.hashtag.subset), verbose = FALSE) %>% 
                      RunPCA(features = rownames(mg1.hashtag.subset), approx = FALSE) %>%
                      RunTSNE(dims = 1:8, perplexity = 100, check_duplicates = FALSE)
mg2.hashtag.subset <- ScaleData(mg2.hashtag.subset, features = rownames(mg2.hashtag.subset), verbose = FALSE) %>% 
                      RunPCA(features = rownames(mg2.hashtag.subset), approx = FALSE) %>%
                      RunTSNE(dims = 1:8, perplexity = 100, check_duplicates = FALSE)

# One can also visualize the more detailed classification result by running Idents(object) <- 'HTO_classification' before plotting. 
# Here, one can see that each of the small clouds on the tSNE plot corresponds to one of the 28 possible doublet combinations.
Idents(mg1.hashtag.subset) <- 'hash.ID' 
Idents(mg2.hashtag.subset) <- 'hash.ID' 
( DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10)) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10)) )

pdf("Plots/Protocol_optimization/umap_HTOs_singlets.pdf", width = 9, height = 5)
( DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10), pt.size = 0.4) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10), pt.size = 0.4) )
dev.off()

png("Plots/Protocol_optimization/umap_HTOs_singlets.png", width = 4200, height = 2200, res = 480)
( DimPlot(mg1.hashtag.subset, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10), pt.size = 0.4) | DimPlot(mg2.hashtag.subset, cols = vintage_rich_cols(10), pt.size = 0.4) )
dev.off()

```
